verdict.rationale: Evidence shows reference documentation exists broadly across many AWS services—compute, storage, database, NoSQL, IAM, CLI, CloudFormation, CDK, Cost Explorer, Bedrock—via docs.aws.amazon.com and a structured llms.txt index (aws-docs-36 to aws-docs-42, aws-probe-1), suggesting wide per-service doc coverage rather than only flagship services. However, there's no evidence assessing actual consistency/quality parity of API/CLI reference docs between major and minor/niche services, no OpenAPI spec found (aws-probe-3 returns 404s), and community comments note AWS's documentation/naming can be confusing (aws-comm-10, aws-comm-11) though this doesn't concretely dispute reference-doc coverage. Missing for 10: direct evidence comparing doc depth/format consistency across obscure vs flagship services, machine-readable API spec coverage, and independent corroboration that lesser-used services have equally thorough references.
